author: Literature Devil
description:
What does Berserk teach us about the true nature of evil? Through Griffith, Guts, the God Hand, and the horrifying Eclipse, Kentaro Miura reveals something terrifying about temptation, despair, and the choices that turn ordinary people into monsters.

In this Berserk manga analysis, we explore one of the darkest themes in Kentaro Miura's masterpiece: evil doesn't simply tempt, it waits until they're desperate enough to sacrifice what they love most.

From the tragic fall of the Slug Count and Rosine to Griffith's betrayal during the Eclipse, Berserk demonstrates how suffering, desperation, and the promise of salvation can lead even seemingly good people down the path of damnation.

But is evil truly irresistible when someone has lost everything? And what separates those who surrender to darkness from those who refuse?

We'll examine Berserk's philosophy of evil, morality, sacrifice, and redemption while drawing comparisons to Star Wars, Luke Skywalker's temptation by the Emperor, and
title: What Berserk Teaches Us About Evil
